runs: Choose which runs and references appear in every chart. References only apply to the nowcast charts.
lossscale: Raw shows the loss as logged. Relative divides each run's loss by its own starting loss (start) or by base Chronos-2 on the same blocks (base). The x axis is simulations trained, from each run's own checkpoints and logged chunks, so runs with different steps per simulation line up. Full range (the default) shows every run whole; live run zooms to the current run.
train: Quantile (pinball) loss on the training batches, as a rolling mean of 20 logged points. Lower is better. Faint dots are the live run's single logged values. Run colours are in the selector at the top.
held: The loss on the full held-out (validation) set, which the model never trains on, at step 0 (base Chronos-2) and at each checkpoint. Lower is better. Loss type picks the whole loss, its nowcast part (the steps from each block's start to its cut-off) or forecast part (the steps after it), which sum to the loss, or the loss by layout or by level, all from the same full evaluation. Relative to start divides by step 0; relative to base Chronos-2 by the base run's step 0.
losstype: Which validation loss the validation panel shows, for every selected run, from the full held-out set at step 0 and each checkpoint: total; the nowcast steps (from the start of each block's window to its cut-off) or the forecast steps after it; by data layout; or by level (national, intermediate, leaf). By layout and by level, colour is the layout or level and line style the run.
biasline: Each line is one layer's bias for that relation, its mean over the 12 heads, against simulations trained. Shallow layers are light and deep ones dark, in the relation's colour (the layer key above). One panel per relation, all on one scale. With several runs selected, the layers are those of the run picked above the panels; each other run is one line, its mean over layers and heads, in its line style. Each run's values are its own: its history, its checkpoints' adapters and its logged means; a run with none is listed as missing. Hover a line for its layer, simulations and value.
biasheat: One square per layer (row) x head (column), the latest saved values of the run named above the panels, on one scale for every relation (the key above). Orange means that head attends more than base Chronos-2 to that kind of pair, blue less. A bias of 1 weights those pairs x2.7.
relations: same = a place's counts, lags and totals. up = a place to its country. down = a country to its places. self = a row with itself, shown only for runs that train it.
lr: Learning rate of each optimiser group. Each run is drawn against simulations trained: the rate falls linearly to zero at the run's last simulation. The dot marks where the run is now.
perf: WIS or CRPS relative to randomwalknowcast. Below 1 is better. One line per run across checkpoints, with the zero-shot and randomwalknowcast references.
nowcast: One nowcast date: the median and 50% and 90% bands of each ticked run for the chosen date, against the truth (95% where the forecasts stop at the 2.5% and 97.5% quantiles, as the German hub's do); line style runs from dotted (earliest checkpoint) to solid (latest). Nowcasts over time: one model's nowcasts from several origins on one plot, each with its horizons, against the final truth (the latest release where there is one), as in the paper's nowcasts-over-time panel. The slider and buttons move the latest origin; Origins and every set how many and how far apart.
wis: Mean score over the nowcast dates the ticked runs have in common: weighted interval score for quantile forecasts, sample CRPS for sample forecasts. Lower is better. Each WIS bar is split into dispersion (interval width), overprediction (truth below the intervals) and underprediction (truth above), shades of the row's colour as in the paper; hover a part for its value.
logwis: The same WIS on the log scale: of log(x + 1) of the truth and of each quantile, as the shared scorer takes log WIS. It weighs relative errors, so small and large counts count alike. Split into the same three parts.
coverage: Share of truths inside the 50% and 90% intervals, as in the paper. The 90% interval needs the 5% and 95% quantiles: sample-based datasets give them, but the German hub's quantiles stop at 2.5% and 97.5%, so German rows use the 95% interval. The dashed lines mark the nominal levels.
biasscore: Mean of 1 minus 2 times the forecast CDF at the truth, from -1 (forecast too low) to +1 (too high). 0 is unbiased.
t_step: The trainer's current optimiser step and simulations trained, from its status file.
t_rate: Training speed from the trainer's timestamped steps: each logged step and its status file, which it writes every few steps. Over the last hour, or the last two points if they are further apart (evaluations log a step only every few hundred). Since the last restart only. Below: the mean over the whole run (leaving out stops of over half an hour).
t_next: Simulations trained so far of the next checkpoint's size, and when it is due: the simulations still to go at the run's steps a simulation so far, at the steps a second since the last restart. A checkpoint already written and still being scored at its size is named below with the time it was written.
t_eta: Time to the final checkpoint, worked out as for the next checkpoint.
t_lr: Current learning rate of each optimiser group.
t_trainer: Whether the trainer process is running.
t_log: Time of the last training log line. It turns red after 10 minutes.
wissplit: Each model's mean WIS over the common nowcast dates, as the other score panels, split by the part of the horizon: the nowcast part, reference dates up to the nowcast date (solid), and the forecast part, reference dates after it, by week ahead (cross-hatched). The same split as the validation loss and the paper. A dataset whose targets end at the nowcast date (the German hub's, 28 days back to the nowcast date) has no forecast part.
t_tput: Throughput from the trainer's stored chunk timings, kept across restarts, else its chunk-time lines: each finished chunk's waiting for batches, cutting blocks, training and evaluating time. Steps and simulations over that time only, so a restart or a pause between chunks does not count. A chunk a restart resumed part way counts only the steps it trained after the restart, and that share of its simulations. GPU busy is the share spent training and evaluating; waiting and cutting run on the CPU. This segment is the running segment's log; whole run is every segment's, a chunk logged twice counted once.
t_now: What the trainer is doing now, from its status file: its stage and, while a chunk trains, that chunk's simulations, the steps done of it (the step less the chunk's first step, from where the trainer last resumed) and the time left at the current steps a second.
t_timings: One row a checkpoint, for the segment of simulations it adds. Steps: the checkpoint's steps less the previous checkpoint's (the training segment's: so far). Steps timed: the share of them the trainer's stored timings time (train/timings/n<N>.json, kept across restarts), or for a run that kept none, the segment's log; there a restart wrote the log again, so the chunks before it are lost, and a chunk it resumed part way is timed only after the restart. Training time: the timed chunks' own time (waiting, cutting blocks, training, evaluating), not wall time; when only part is timed it is scaled up to all the steps at the timed rate and marked ≈. Simulations/h: over the timed part. Wall time: from the previous checkpoint's save to this one's, restarts and idle time included. Saved: when the trainer saved the checkpoint. Released: when it was published as a release.
validation: Each checkpoint's and base Chronos-2's forecasts of a fixed sample of the run's held-out (validation) blocks, one block and row at a time: black is the block's history and truth, each model its median with 50% and 95% bands. The dashed line is the cut-off: steps before it are nowcasts, after it forecasts. Written after each checkpoint at low priority, so they lag the losses.
lorasize: How far the LoRA adapter has moved the model from base Chronos-2: the Frobenius norm of each module's scaled update B·A, a layer's q, k, v and o projections added in quadrature. Against simulations trained, one line per encoder layer, shallow light to deep dark in the kind's colour: time attention (along each series), group attention (across the series of a block) and the output layer. The four panels of this row share one scale. With several runs selected, the layers are those of the run picked above the grid; each other run is one dashed line, its root mean square over layers. It shows where the model changes, not whether it improves.
loraproj: The update size of each attention projection (query q, key k, value v, output o), its root mean square over the time and group attention sublayers of every layer, against simulations trained, on the row's scale.
lorachange: How much each layer's update moved between checkpoints: the Frobenius norm of the change in B·A since the previous checkpoint over the norm of the update now, a layer's projections in quadrature. One square per layer (row) and checkpoint (column, named by its simulations), darker for more change, on one scale for time and group attention (the key above). 1 means the segment moved the layer as far as its whole update; values falling towards 0 mean the layer is settling.
lorarank: The effective rank of each layer's update at the last checkpoint, the mean over its q, k, v and o projections: the exponential of the entropy of the shares of its squared singular values. 1 means the update uses one direction; the adapter's rank (r) means it spreads evenly over all of them.
loraab: The Frobenius norms of the LoRA factors at the last checkpoint by layer, a layer's projections in quadrature: A (solid) maps the input down to rank r and starts random; B (dashed) maps it back up and starts at zero, so B's growth is the update's.
